title: Compatible Euler-tours
exact_target:
Does an Eulerian graph of minimum degree $2d$ always have at least
$2d-2$ Euler tours sharing no local edge transition?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Let $G$ be a finite connected loopless graph with every degree positive
and even, and let its minimum degree be $2d$. Distinct parallel edges,
if allowed, are treated as distinct objects. An Euler tour is a closed
walk using every edge exactly once. At each visit to a vertex it pairs
the entering edge with the leaving edge; the final and initial edges
are paired too. These unordered pairs are its transitions.

Two Euler tours are compatible when they have no transition in common
at any vertex. Let $q(G)$ be the greatest size of a family whose tours
are pairwise compatible. The conjectured bound is
\[
                         2d-2\le q(G)\le2d-1.
\]
Thus the substantive assertion asks for at least $2d-2$ mutually
compatible tours, for every such graph. At a vertex of degree $2d$, each
tour uses $d$ distinct pairs from the $\binom{2d}{2}$ possible pairs,
explaining the upper bound.

Tours are considered as cyclic edge traversals: rotating the start point
or reversing a traversal does not provide a new transition system.
Pairwise compatibility is a simultaneous requirement among all tours.
Constructing a tour compatible with one previously chosen tour does
not automatically construct a family of the required cardinality.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Does an Eulerian graph of minimum degree $2d$ always have at least
$2d-2$ Euler tours sharing no local edge transition?
